classification.difficultyReason: Classify six named angles using intersecting straight lines and a supplied right-angle mark.

content.prompt: In the diagram opposite, state whether the following angles are acute, obtuse, right or straight.

spec.sourceRegion: Chapter 7 review question 1, diagram at right
spec.description: Three straight lines A–G–D, E–G–B and F–G–C intersect at G. A and B lie above G, E and D below G. A right-angle square marks angle AGB. All six peripheral points retain visible markers. Decorative blue lines and red markers are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AG is perpendicular to GB; opposite rays are GA/GD, GE/GB and GF/GC. The horizontal line lies between the diagonal rays on either side.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no classifications or numerical angle answers appear.

answer.worked: $\angle BGC$ is less than $90^\circ$, so it is acute.
$\angle AGE$ and the marked right angle $\angle AGB$ are adjacent angles on the straight line $EGB$. Thus $\angle AGE=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ$, so it is right.
$\angle FGD$ is greater than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$, so it is obtuse.
$E$, $G$ and $B$ lie on one straight line, with $G$ between $E$ and $B$. Hence $\angle EGB=180^\circ$, so it is straight.
$\angle CGD$ is less than $90^\circ$, so it is acute.
$\angle EGD$ is vertically opposite the marked right angle $\angle AGB$. Thus $\angle EGD=90^\circ$, so it is right.
